title: Process Tree Investigation
description: Analyze a given process tree and identify the malicious parent-child anomaly.
problemStatement:
### Scenario
You are investigating an alert from a workstation. The EDR provides the following process creation timeline (simplified).

```
Time    | Parent Process           | Child Process
--------|--------------------------|---------------------------
10:01 AM| explorer.exe             | OUTLOOK.EXE
10:02 AM| OUTLOOK.EXE              | WINWORD.EXE
10:02 AM| WINWORD.EXE              | cmd.exe
10:03 AM| cmd.exe                  | powershell.exe
10:03 AM| powershell.exe           | rundll32.exe
10:04 AM| rundll32.exe             | (Network connection to 185.142.53.21:443)
```

### Questions
1.  Identify **TWO** suspicious parent-child relationships in this chain.
2.  What likely triggered this chain? (Hint: Look at the first parent).
3.  What is the final outcome of this chain?
4.  If you could isolate one Event ID (from Windows Logs) to investigate further, which would it be?
hints: Remember that Office applications (Outlook, Word) should never spawn command shells (cmd.exe).
PowerShell spawning rundll32.exe with a network connection is a common way to load shellcode.
expectedOutput: 1. WINWORD.EXE -> cmd.exe (Macro execution). powershell.exe -> rundll32.exe (LOLBin execution). 2. A malicious email attachment or link opened in Outlook that launched a Word document with macros. 3. Code execution and likely establishing a C2 connection to the attacker's IP. 4. Event ID 4688 (Process Creation) to see the full command line arguments.
